text:
Logan Cooley was the hottest player on a cold Utah team before he got hurt: 13 points in his last ten games, 10 of them goals, including a pair of hat tricks in Pittsburgh and Montreal. He's missed the last few games and is now listed day-to-day, and the Mammoth haven't won without him.

The hot streak is earned, not just lucky. He's getting more chances than usual, 4.6 expected goals (the quality of chances) on his own shots over those ten games against 3.5 normally, and Utah takes 58% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on the ice. But 11 goals on 6.3 expected means he's shooting 35%, against 24% last season, and nobody keeps that up. Expect fewer goals and the same player. Our talent range projects about 77 points.

What makes him dangerous is how he gets there. He's in the 99th percentile for top skating speed by NHL EDGE, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in on 56% of his entries last season, with 85th-percentile shot assists. Our closest comparison is his own teammate Nick Schmaltz. At 22, the third overall pick from 2022 is turning into the player Utah drafted.
